candidate.scope: Single linear Illumina component schematic labeled DNase I hypersensitive sites sequencing (DNase-Seq), catalogued as DNase-Seq/DNasel-Seq: active chromatin -> DNase I digestion -> isolate trimmed complexes -> DNA extraction -> DNA. The title spellings are co-labels at this schematic scope, not evidence for two implementations. The far-left highlighted chromatin icon is an assay overview, not an upstream transformation. operations.label: DNase I digestion
operations.description: Treat active chromatin (DNA-protein complexes) with DNase I. Accessible DNA is cleaved, and the drawing proceeds toward shorter, separated protein-associated DNA complexes. This preserves the figure's trimming/protection depiction; primary DNase-seq interpretation relies on the locations of DNase-created DNA ends.
operations.mechanism: DNase I endonuclease cleavage depends on DNA accessibility. Protein-associated regions may be relatively protected; nucleosomal DNA is not absolutely resistant. The yellow digestion-stage symbols are treated as reagent/action icons, not as tagged products.
operations.information_effect: Cleavage positions on genomic DNA encode local DNase sensitivity. Primary DNase-seq maps these positions to infer accessible regulatory regions. A resistance footprint is an inference from local cleavage depletion, not proof of a specific bound protein or complete regulatory-site coverage.
